L17: # Lake Louise and Moraine Lake
L18: ## Banff National Park
L19: 
L20: Lake Louise and Moraine Lake are among the most visited destinations in Canada. It's not hard to see why! Extensive hiking trails wrap bright blue lakes, offering breathtaking vistas at every turn. The best way to see Lake Louise and Moraine Lake is on cite5†Parks Canada shuttles or cite6†Roam Public Transit†roamtransit.com . cite7†Parking is limited in the Lake Louise area .
L21: Location: 55 km west of the Town of Banff, Alberta, on the Trans-Canada Highway 1.
L22: Founded in 1890 as Laggan Station, Lake Louise was once a wild outpost at the end of the Canadian Pacific Railway. Today the Community of Lake Louise, the lake, and the surrounding area offer some of the finest hiking, skiing and site-seeing in the world. Lake Louise and Moraine Lake usually melt by late May. Alpine hiking season begins in late June.
L23: ### Heads up! Due to high demand, visiting Lake Louise and Moraine Lake requires planning.
L24: 
L25: Parking lots fill up before sunrise and remain full until sunset. Taking transit or booking a Parks Canada shuttle is easy, stress-free and the only way to guarantee you can see these two lakes. Reserving your shuttle in advance is required.
L26: #### cite5†Parks Canada shuttles: L27: 
L28: Reserving a seat on a Parks Canada shuttle is the best way to make the most of your time in the Lake Louise area and guarantees the ability to see both lakes in one day! Reserve your shuttle ticket online and park your vehicle at the Lake Louise Park and Ride, located at the Lake Louise Ski Resort. cite8†Click here for directions†www.google.ca .
L29: 
L30: Additional seats will be made available for reservation at 8 am MDT, two days prior to departure.
L31: cite6†Roam Public Transit†roamtransit.com can also be used to travel from the Town of Banff to the Community of Lake Louise.
L32:

L35: cite10†Reserve now†reservation.pc.gc.ca L36: #### cite7†Parking in the Lake Louise area: L37: 
L38: Parking in the Community of Lake Louise is limited.
L39: 
L40: Paid parking is in effect at Lake Louise lakeshore during the shuttle season. Visit our cite11†fees page for pricing.
L41: 
L42: cite9†Learn more L43: 
L44: * * *
L45: 
L46: When to visit
L47: 
L48: Lake Louise is one of Canada’s most popular destinations. Planning ahead is essential!
L49: 
L50: Lake Louise: The Community of Lake Louise and the Lake Louise Lakeshore are open year-round.
L51: Moraine Lake: Moraine Lake Road is closed to personal vehicles year-round. Parks Canada shuttles and licensed commercial vehicle operators with a Moraine Lake Road Licence of Occupation are permitted from June to mid-October. Exact dates are weather dependent. Exceptions will be made for visitors with valid, government-issued accessible parking placards and registered guests of Moraine Lake Lodge.
L52: During the winter, the road is track-set for skiing and the lake itself is inaccessible due to avalanche hazard.
L53: cite12†Seasonal closures and restrictions L54: 
L55: From May through October, Lake Louise and Moraine Lake are extremely busy. Expect full parking lots, traffic control personnel, traffic congestion, long waits, and paid parking. Visitors are encouraged to plan ahead and have a backup plan.
L56:   * Reservations for cite13†campsites in the Lake Louise area begin in January and shuttle reservations begin in April.
L57:   * Visitors looking to experience Lake Louise and Moraine Lake throughout the summer should start their planning now. Explore our “cite9†Visiting Lake Louise and Moraine Lake " page now to plan your transit in advance.
L58:   * When possible, visitors are encouraged to leave their vehicles at home and take transit from either Calgary, Banff or Lake Louise. cite14†Click here for more information .
L59: When are Lake Louise and Moraine Lake busiest?
L60: Holidays and weekends are especially busy, including:
L61: 
L62:   * Victoria Day (May, date varies by year)
L63:   * Canada Day (July 1)
L64:   * Heritage Day (first Monday in August)
L65:   * Labour Day (first Monday in September)
L66:   * Larch season (weekends in September)
L67: 
L68: From November through April, Lake Louise is a winter wonderland! We receive more snow than other parts of Banff National Park and are proud to have one of the longest ski seasons in North America.
L69: 
L70: The busiest weekends during the winter are:
L71:   * Boxing Day through New Year (December 26 to January 1)
L72:   * Ice Magic Festival (January, dates vary by year)
L73:   * Family Day (second Monday in February)
L74:   * Easter weekend (dates vary by year)
L75: 
L76: How to get there
L77: 
L78: There are multiple ways to access Lake Louise and Moraine Lake, including shuttles, transit, biking and travelling by foot. Learn more cite9†here .
L79: Important information: Moraine Lake is considered backcountry. If you choose to bike there, you must be prepared to be self-sufficient. There is no cell service, Wi-Fi, running water or other services including lighting along the road. Pit toilets are available at the lake. There is cell phone reception is available approximately 5 km away from the lake on Moraine Lake Road.
L80: 
L81: Things to do
L82: Lake Louise and Moraine Lake usually melt by late May. Alpine hiking season begins in late June. Ski season begins in mid-November.
L83: 
L84:   * cite15†Hiking L85:   * cite16†Biking L86:   * cite17†Skiing and Snowshoeing L87:   * cite18†Wildlife watching L88: 
L89: Every destination in the Lake Louise area is beautiful but only some are open year-round. This is when the most popular local destinations are open:
L90:   * Lake Louise lakeshore (year-round)
L91:   * Community of Lake Louise (year-round)
L92:   * Moraine Lake (early-June to mid-October)
L93:   * Lake Louise Ski Resort (November to May)
L94:   * Summer Gondola at the Lake Louise Ski Resort (mid-May to mid-October)
L95: When do the teahouses open at Lake Louise?
L96: The charming Lake Agnes and Plain of Six Glaciers tea houses are the most popular summer hiking destinations in the Lake Louise area. These privately operated teahouses open mid-May and close after Canadian Thanksgiving in mid-October.
L97: 
L98: The hikes to the teahouses are not safe from November through mid-May due to avalanche hazard. Do not hike to Lake Agnes or to the Plain of Six Glacier during the winter or spring. In May and June, check the trail report before departing.

L105: 
L106: In Canada, national parks enjoy special protections that may differ from other protected places. Please know “what not to do” in a national park.

L113: 
L114: Walking, snowshoeing or tobogganing? You don’t need to venture far to be in avalanche terrain. November through June, not all sign-posted destinations are safe for travel. Choose your winter destination from a list of designated trails.

It is located in the heart of the Community of Lake Louise. Parking for vehicles and RVs is available in the Samson Mall parking lot. A small grocery store, outdoor store, cafés, book store, post office and bank machine are also available here.
